questions.question_text:
The vector $\underset{\sim}{q}$ is written as the ordered pair $(-5,-2)$.
Which is $\underset{\sim}{q}$ in component form?

options.why: Took the second number of the pair as the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component.
Kept the correct order but dropped the negative on the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component.
Reversed the order of the pair and also dropped a negative sign.

questions.solution_text:
The first number of $(x,y)$ is the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component.
$(-5,-2)$
$=-5\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{j}$

questions.question_text: Write $7\underset{\sim}{i}-3\underset{\sim}{k}$ as a column vector in three dimensions.

options.why: Put the $\underset{\sim}{k}$ component in the middle row, which belongs to $\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Placed the components in the correct rows but dropped the negative sign on the $\underset{\sim}{k}$ term.
Both put the $\underset{\sim}{k}$ component in the middle row and dropped the negative sign.

questions.solution_text:
There is no $\underset{\sim}{j}$ term, so the middle component is $0$.
$7\underset{\sim}{i}-3\underset{\sim}{k}$
$=\begin{pmatrix}7\\0\\-3\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question_text:
Three of these are the same vector written in different forms.
Which one is **not** equal to $-8\underset{\sim}{k}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$?

options.why: This column lists the components $0$, $5$ and $-8$ in order from top to bottom, so it is equal to the given vector.
The terms are printed with $\underset{\sim}{j}$ first, but the coefficients still match $0\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}-8\underset{\sim}{k}$.
An ordered triple lists the $x$-, $y$- and $z$-components in order, so it is equal to the given vector.

questions.solution_text:
$-8\underset{\sim}{k}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$ has $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component $0$, $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component $5$, and $\underset{\sim}{k}$ component $-8$.
$-8\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$ has $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component $-8$, $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component $5$, and $\underset{\sim}{k}$ component $0$.
The unit vectors do not match, so $-8\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$ is not equal to the given vector.
